caseno: Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 46 of 1989. with Suo Moto Rule No.47 of 1989.
lawyer:
Abdul Malek with Mainul Hosein, Joynal Abedin, Advocates ---------- For the Petitioner. 
B. Hossain, D.A.G. with A.K.M. Shamsul Karim, A.A.G ---------- For the State. 
Aminul Huq with Nizamul Huque, Advocates ---------- For the Complaint.
parties:
Shah Alam Chowdhury --------------- Petitioner
Vs.
The State ---------- Opposite Party.
full_judgment: "The law does not debar a Police Officer from resuming investigation and submitting fresh charge-sheet although a final report had earlier been submitted in the case. The fresh charge-sheet would be police report as contemplated under section 173 of the Code. Since clause (b) of subsection (1) of section 190 of the Code empowers a Magistrate to take cognizance on a Police report, it does not appear how a Magistrate can be prevented from taking cognizance on a Police report submitted after fresh investigation into a case (Reference: Jiban Krishna Samanta Vs. State I.L.R. (1950) 2 Ca1.66; A.K. Roy Vs. State of West Bengal, A.I.R. 1962 Calcutta (F.13.) 135) In the instant case the learned Magistrate did not take cognizance on the basis of the earlier Police report which resulted in the discharge of the petitioner and hence the question of revival of proceedings against the petitioner, raised by Mr. Hasan Arif, does not arise. The cognizance against the petitioner was taken on the basis of the subsequent police report, which resulted in charge-sheet being submitted against him and as such the question of having first the earlier order of discharge set aside by a superior Court, as raised further by Mr. Hasan Arif, does not also arise. We, therefore,   see no reason for interference with the order taking cognizance against the petitioner."
